Compare the small sausage-shaped organelles with inner membranes to what a chloroplast should look like. Can you see any large organelle with stacked thylakoids, and can you see tiny dots and channels in the walls?
walkthrough:
**Recognise it is a plant cell**

This is a plant cell because you can see a rigid cell wall all around, large vacuoles, and a large central nucleus. That already makes plasmodesmata (channels through plant walls) likely.

**Spot the easy visible structures**

The nucleus contains a very dark, dense nucleolus (1). The cytoplasm is full of tiny dark dots, the ribosomes (4). The elongated organelles with folded inner membranes are mitochondria (5), not chloroplasts.

**Rule out what is missing**

There is no large chloroplast (2) with grana and thylakoids visible here. There are also no clearly resolvable microtubules (3), which are only about 25 nm wide. Small breaks across the wall on the left are plasmodesmata (6). So 1, 4, 5 and 6 are seen.

options.A: Includes chloroplast and microtubules which are not clearly visible, and misses mitochondria and plasmodesmata which are visible.
options.B: Correctly identifies the dark nucleolus, tiny ribosomes, small mitochondria with cristae, and plasmodesmata in the plant cell walls.
options.C: Wrong because it includes chloroplast and microtubules which cannot be seen, and misses nucleolus and ribosomes which can.
options.D: Wrong because it includes chloroplast which is absent, even though ribosomes, mitochondria and plasmodesmata are correctly spotted.
